articles.headline: One 75-Minute Weekly Session Cuts Belly Fat Better Than You'd Think
articles.body: <cite index="1-2">A four-month study found that completing 75 minutes of brisk interval walking in a single weekly session reduced body fat, trimmed waistlines, and improved cardiovascular fitness about as effectively as splitting the same exercise across three days.</cite> For busy professionals juggling a hundred priorities, this hits different. You don't need to carve out time every day. Concentrate your effort once a week. The metabolic payoff stays the same. This works especially well if you're carrying excess weight around your midsection—the type that matters most for heart health.
articles.takeaway: One focused 75-minute interval walk per week can deliver the same body composition and fitness gains as three spread-out sessions. Time is no excuse.

articles.topic: Gut bacteria Roseburia and muscle strength
articles.headline: This Gut Bacterium Could Be Your Secret Strength Edge
articles.body: <cite index="36-1,36-2">Scientists have linked a specific gut bacterium, Roseburia inulinivorans, to stronger muscles in both humans and mice. Older adults who carried it had 29% greater handgrip strength, while treated mice gained about 30% more grip strength.</cite> <cite index="36-18">The bacterium may increase the proportion of fast-twitch (type II) fibers, which are important for short bursts of intense activity such as sprinting and weightlifting.</cite> Your gut isn't just digesting food. It's quietly governing how much strength your muscles can generate. Feed the right microbes, and your hands grip harder. Your legs push stronger.
articles.takeaway: A single gut bacterium shows direct links to muscle strength—suggesting the microbiome is a legitimate performance lever, not just a health buzzword.

articles.headline: Seven Days of Meditation Rewires Your Brain—Without Drugs
articles.body: <cite index="44-1,44-3">An intensive seven-day meditation retreat triggered striking changes across the brain and body, including shifts tied to neuroplasticity, immunity, metabolism, and natural pain relief. Participants also showed brain connectivity patterns resembling those associated with psychedelic experiences, suggesting that powerful altered states may be achievable without drugs.</cite> You don't need a week in isolation to start seeing results. But carving out time to sit still and focus inward does something real to your nervous system. Your brain gets quieter. Your body recovers faster. The effects compound over time.
articles.takeaway: One week of immersive meditation produces measurable changes in brain connectivity and function—comparable to non-ordinary states of consciousness.

articles.topic: Low-fat vegan diet energy density and weight loss
articles.headline: Eat More Food, Lose Weight—Without Counting Calories
articles.body: <cite index="61-1,61-3">In a 16-week clinical trial, people eating mostly fruits, vegetables, grains, and legumes consumed about 357 fewer calories per day even though the total amount of food they ate barely changed.</cite> <cite index="66-5,66-6">Calorie-dense animal foods such as meat, dairy and eggs were eliminated, while intake of high-volume, low-energy-density plant foods—especially vegetables and legumes—rose sharply. Because these foods carry few calories per gram, participants could eat generous portions while consuming less energy overall.</cite> Stop fighting hunger. Swap what's on your plate instead. Your stomach stays full. Your body naturally eats less.
articles.takeaway: Shifting to plant-based whole foods cuts energy density by roughly 30%—allowing people to eat satisfying portions while automatically reducing calorie intake.
articles.source: JAMA Network Open / Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine

workout.title: Hinge, Squat & Press: Lower-Body Power in 30
workout.tip: If your lower back rounds at the bottom of a Romanian deadlift, shorten your range of motion. Control beats depth every time, especially when you're tired at rep 10.
workout.warmup: Spend 3 minutes doing bodyweight leg swings, hip circles, and slow air squats to 90 degrees. Finish with 10 glute bridges on the floor to activate the posterior chain before you load it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Hinge at the hips, not the waist. Feel the hamstrings load before you drive back up. Keep the dumbbells close to your legs throughout.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat with Pause
exercises.notes: Hold one dumbbell at your chest. Pause for 2 seconds at the bottom of each rep. This kills momentum and forces real quad and glute work.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge with Knee Drive
exercises.notes: Step back and lower your rear knee toward the floor, then drive the rear knee forward as you return to standing. Works balance, glutes, and hip flexors in one shot.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Lie on your back, one foot flat on the floor. Drive through that heel to lift your hips. Squeeze hard at the top for one second. Use a dumbbell across your hip for more resistance.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
exercises.notes: Wide stance, toes turned out 30 to 45 degrees. Hold one dumbbell with both hands between your legs. Drive your knees out and sit deep. Great for inner thighs and glutes.

workout.cooldown: Finish with 60 seconds of standing quad stretch per leg and a 90-second seated figure-four glute stretch on each side. Your hips will thank you tomorrow.

Pause for 2 seconds at the bottom of each rep. This kills momentum and forces real quad and glute work. Reverse Lunge with Knee Drive: 3 sets x 8 each leg — Step back and lower your rear knee toward the floor, then drive the rear knee forward as you return to standing. Works balance, glutes, and hip flexors in one shot. Single-Leg Glute Bridge: 3 sets x 12 each leg — Lie on your back, one foot flat on the floor. Drive through that heel to lift your hips. Squeeze hard at the top for one second. Use a dumbbell across your hip for more resistance. Dumbbell Sumo Squat: 3 sets x 12 — Wide stance, toes turned out 30 to 45 degrees. Hold one dumbbell with both hands between your legs. Drive your knees out and sit deep. Great for inner thighs and glutes.
